# 8 Best MiniMax M3.1 Flash Alternatives with Benchmarks

Compare 8 MiniMax M3.1 Flash alternatives on AI/ML API: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, Claude Haiku 5.5 and more, with prices and our test.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash is a new low-cost reasoning model built for coding and AI agents, but it's not necessarily the best fit for every task. Depending on your workload, other models may offer faster responses, lower costs, or more reliable results.

To see how they compare, we tested eight MiniMax M3.1 Flash alternatives across 10 coding, agent, and vision tasks, measuring accuracy, response speed, and cost. Here's how each model performed and where it makes sense to use one over MiniMax. [...] Best for: Low-latency requests and video input.

MiMo V2.6 Flash is Xiaomi's open-weight multimodal reasoning model, released under the MIT license. It supports text, images, and video, making it the only MiniMax alternative in this comparison with video input available through AI/ML API.

MiMo is also inexpensive to run, with an output price of just $0.385 per million tokens.

### MiMo V2.6 Flash vs MiniMax M3.1 Flash

MiMo had the lowest task completion rate in our tests, passing only 10 out of 30 runs. Its biggest problems were with coding and agent workflows, where it frequently failed to follow requirements or complete all necessary steps.

## What Is MiniMax M3.1 Flash?

MiniMax M3.1 Flash is the Chinese AI company’s next-generation “Flash” model, the lighter, faster sibling line that sits alongside MiniMax’s larger flagship models. According to the company’s own release announcement, M3.1 Flash is built for agentic tasks, coding, Computer Use, and cybersecurity workloads, the same category of work that has become the proving ground for most frontier labs this year as enterprises push past chatbot use cases into models that take actions, call tools, and operate browsers and terminals on their own. [...] Is the connection between Space Bunny Alpha and M3.1 Flash fully confirmed?  
MiniMax has confirmed that its own internally tracked “Space Bunny” was an early version of M3.1 Flash. Some reporting on a separately labeled “Space Bunny Alpha” model seen on third-party routing platforms has not been definitively confirmed by MiniMax to be identical in every respect, so that specific detail should be treated as unconfirmed.

The Shattered Newsletter: the week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security. [...] What is Space Bunny, and how is it connected to M3.1 Flash?  
Space Bunny was an anonymous model that processed more than 200 trillion tokens while operating under that pseudonym. MiniMax confirmed Space Bunny was an early version of MiniMax M3.1 Flash, revealing the connection as part of the October 19 launch announcement.

How much does MiniMax M3.1 Flash cost?  
MiniMax’s official API pricing is $0.15 per 1 million input tokens and $0.60 per 1 million output tokens, with cached-read tokens priced at $0.015 per 1 million tokens. MiniMax says this reflects a 70% reduction in usage costs compared with its prior Flash generation.

results.title: MiniMax's new M3.1 Flash beats DeepSeek and Opus 5 on a key business benchmark at lower cost — but with a high hallucination rate
results.content:
MiniMax is offering M3.1 Flash through its first-party API, M Plan subscription offering and MiniMax Code desktop application.

The model costs $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, with cached input discounted to just $0.015 per million tokens.

At those rates, a workload consuming one million uncached input tokens and producing one million output tokens would cost $0.75 in model usage charges, excluding other infrastructure or application expenses.

This makes M3.1 Flash among the cheapest frontier AI models in currently available around the world. [...] That represents a substantial improvement in measured capabilities while also taking the average cost of completing an Intelligence Index task from approximately $0.51 down to just $0.22 — a reduction of nearly 57%.

Its closest competitors include GLM-5.3 Flash, which scores 42 at approximately $0.28 per task; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017, which scores 45 at approximately $0.26 per task; and Gemini 3.8 Flash, which scores 41 at approximately $1.24 per task.

While M3.1 Flash remains behind the most capable frontier systems from Anthropic and OpenAI on the overall index, its combination of relatively strong performance and low operating costs makes it an attractive candidate for businesses running AI systems that execute large numbers of tasks.
